extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and applicants (ASEAN member states); patent attorneys and office staff involved in examination and search
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for patent examination focusing on sufficiency of disclosure/enablement, best mode/support/clarity issues, and procedures and standards for conducting patent searches (scope, databases, strategies, and determination of closest prior art).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure (general requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: On filing their application, applicants must supply a sufficient disclosure in respect of the invention as claimed with regard to all of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclosure must enable a person skilled in the art (PSIA) to carry out the invention; insufficient disclosure cannot be cured after filing by adding new examples or features that introduce added subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter-defined claims — methods to determine parameter values
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claims define the invention, or a feature thereof, in terms of parameters, the application as filed must include a clear description of the methods used to determine the parameter values, unless a PSIA would know which method to use or unless all methods would yield the same result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear methods/measurements for parameter features in the specification; otherwise objection for insufficiency may arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: No post‑filing cure by added examples
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner considers the disclosure to be insufficient, such a deficiency cannot be cured after the fact by adding further examples or features which will introduce subject-matter extending beyond the content of the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedial action must remain within the content as filed (e.g., restrict claims to embodiments sufficiently described rather than adding new examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for insufficient disclosure via claim restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Insufficient disclosure could be remedied by restricting the claims to correspond to those embodiments which have been sufficiently described, and by deleting the description of the remaining embodiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where disclosure is deficient, applicants should consider limiting claim scope to what was actually described at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection standard — serious doubts and verifiable facts
rubrics_metrics.description: An objection of lack of sufficient disclosure presupposes that there are serious doubts which are substantiated by verifiable facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should base insufficiency objections on concrete, verifiable evidence rather than mere speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to describe function as well as structure
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary for the invention to be described not only in terms of its structure but also in terms of its function, unless the functions of the various parts are immediately apparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions should include how parts operate/achieve effects, particularly where function is not obvious from structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for determining undue experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors to be considered in determining whether undue experimentation is needed to carry out the claimed invention include: (i) the breadth of the claims; (ii) the nature of the invention; (iii) the general knowledge of a person skilled in the art; (iv) the level of predictability in the art; (v) the amount of direction provided in the application, including references to prior art; and (vi) the amount of experimentation required to carry out the claimed invention on the basis of the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess enablement by weighing these six factors (from narrow to broad) to decide if the disclosure suffices or if undue burden is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irreparable insufficiency — dependence on chance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the successful performance of the invention is dependent on chance (results not reproducible or success totally unreliable), there is a failure to satisfy the requirements of disclosure that is essentially irreparable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish this from inventions with occasional failures (acceptable if satisfactory parts can be sorted by nondestructive tests). Example: microbiological processes involving mutations may be problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irreparable insufficiency — impossibility contrary to physical laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Where successful performance of the invention is inherently impossible because it would be contrary to well-established physical laws (e.g., perpetual motion machine), the disclosure requirement is not satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such claims should be rejected as inherently non‑workable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof in sufficiency objections
rubrics_metrics.description: As a rule, the burden of proof in the framework of sufficiency of disclosure lies with the party raising the objection. If there are serious doubts as regards the possibility of performing the invention and repeating it as described, the burden of proof as regards this possibility, or at least a demonstration that success is credible, rests with the applicant or the proprietor of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When examiner raises serious, substantiated doubts, the applicant should provide evidence or demonstration of reproducibility/credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode requirement (where applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some AMS require that the specification sets forth the best mode of carrying out the invention contemplated by the inventor. The best mode requirement imposes an affirmative obligation on the inventor to disclose the best version of the invention known to them at the time the patent application is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The best mode is subjective (what inventor knew as best at filing); there is no obligation to disclose an absolute best beyond what the inventor knew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: enablement vs best mode
rubrics_metrics.description: The enablement requirement pertains to the sufficiency of the disclosure to teach the PSIA to implement the invention, whereas the best mode pertains to the quality of such disclosure and the honesty of the patent applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat enablement (objective) and best mode (subjective/honesty) as separate legal/practical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPS: enablement mandatory, best mode optional
rubrics_metrics.description: TRIPS Article 29(1) requires that an applicant disclose the invention sufficiently clear and complete to be carried out by a PSIA, but the requirement to indicate the best mode is optional for members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National laws must at least implement enablement; best mode inclusion is at member discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient disclosure can undermine claim support
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the disclosure is insufficient to enable a PSIA to carry out the claimed invention, the claims may also be too broad to be supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliance with sufficiency often coincides with lack of support for claims; consider both grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure vs clarity balance
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a delicate balance between lack of clarity and lack of disclosure. An ambiguity in the claims may lead to an objection for lack of disclosure if the whole scope of the claim is affected (impossible to carry out); otherwise an objection under lack of clarity is more appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose objection type depending on whether ambiguity prevents implementation across the claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of trade names/proper names
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of trade mark, company name, trade name or similar words to refer to materials or articles is undesirable insofar as such words merely denote origin or relate to a range of different products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If trade names are used, the product must be sufficiently identified without reliance on the trade name; widely accepted standard names (e.g. 'Bowden' cable) may be allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search objective — discover relevant prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of search is to discover relevant prior art(s): everything capable of being of assistance in determining whether the claimed invention is new and involves an inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searching authority must attempt to discover as much relevant prior art as its facilities permit, including material that assists on sufficiency, support and industrial applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search should cite documents assisting other requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to establish the search report, the searching authority is encouraged to cite prior art documents which may be of assistance in determining whether other requirements, such as sufficiency, support and industrial applicability, are fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite not only novelty/inventive-step hits but also documents useful for assessing enablement/support/applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search completeness and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The search must be as complete and effective as possible, within the limitations necessarily imposed by issues such as unity of invention and other considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise judgement about feasible scope given resources and procedural constraints; do not omit necessary fields without justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search normally by one examiner; multiple examiners when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: The search itself is normally performed by one examiner but in appropriate cases where the invention requires searching in widely dispersed specialized fields, a search report containing the work of two or more examiners may be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-examiner searches for multi-disciplinary or widely dispersed technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide written opinion with search report (best practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practice is when the examiner provides a written opinion on novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability of the claimed invention at the same time as producing the search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A timely written opinion helps applicants know how to amend applications to overcome objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search basis — use search copy and prohibit amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the search has started, or after the request for search/examination has been submitted, there is no right of amending the application until after the search has been established; consequently the search must be carried out on the basis of the search copy of the application as submitted to the patent office. The only exception is that obvious mistakes may be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on amendments to expand/alter the search basis; correct only obvious errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search options and language considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Search options, preferably online, are critical. Both English and the country's official language should at least be used by AMS patent offices in conducting searches. Additional languages (e.g., Japanese or German) should be used whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multilingual resources and interfaces where available; public access and English interfaces are best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior search/examination reports
rubrics_metrics.description: For priority-based applicants, the applicant may submit earlier search and examination reports and/or written opinions and/or granted patents; the receiving patent office may take those results into account and may invite the applicant to furnish them within a reasonable time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier reports may be considered to replace part of the search if they are of real benefit; examiner should evaluate relevance and fields searched by earlier authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Databases and internet sources in search
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything made available to the public anywhere in the world by written disclosure prior to the relevant date is prior art; internet sources, online journals and databases may need to be used in addition to patent literature and non-patent literature databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search may include both non-commercial (e.g., Espacenet) and commercial databases; internet searches may be necessary especially in information/software-related fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner judgment to omit low-yield segments
rubrics_metrics.description: While the searching authority, in principle, consults all documents within the field of search irrespective of language or age, the examiner should, for reasons of economy, exercise appropriate judgment to omit segments of search files or databases in which the likelihood of finding relevant documents is very small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use experience and technology knowledge to focus effort; justify omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family handling — consult only one member unless differences likely
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner needs to consult only one member of a patent family unless there is good reason to suppose relevant substantial differences in content of different members, or because only another member was published before the filing date and must therefore be cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer earliest/prior member unless others contain materially different disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend search to other resources when justified
rubrics_metrics.description: The search may have to be extended to include other listed resources or databases (e.g., IPDL) or analogous fields, but the need for this must be judged by the examiner in each individual case, taking into account the outcome of the initial search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select additional resources/classifications when initial results indicate their likely relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet search confidentiality caution
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may use the internet as necessary when searching unpublished applications but must take great care not to disclose confidential information through the inadvertent use of search terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select limited, non-disclosing keywords rather than long claim text when searching public internet resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogous fields — when to include
rubrics_metrics.description: The field of search should, where appropriate, include analogous fields to the extent that they are consistent with the description and drawings. Fields regarded as analogous are considered in light of necessary function or use, not only specific functions indicated in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider (i) fields where same/similar structure would be used for different activities, (ii) fields to which a generic concept pertains, (iii) art within inventor's activity relevant to the problem, (iv) fields relevant to function/utility inherent in the claims; extend only when a reasonable objection of lack of inventive step could be established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search parameters and coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The search parameters may cover the International Patent Classification (IPC), keywords and drawings and the search coverage may include abstracts, claims, title, description and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a combination of IPC, keywords, and document parts to capture relevant prior art; emphasize main technical field and most promising strategies first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of the claims for search subject
rubrics_metrics.description: When beginning to search an application, the examiner first considers the application in order to determine the subject of the claimed invention and makes a critical analysis of the claims in light of the description and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search is directed to invention as interpreted with due regard to description/drawings, with particular emphasis on the inventive concept towards which the claims are directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full coverage principle
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, and insofar as possible and reasonable, the search should cover the entire subject-matter to which the claims are directed or to which they might reasonably be expected to be directed after they have been amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where practical, include embodiments/examples in the search even if claims are functional, but consider reasons of economy where breadth and many examples make full coverage impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculative/unduly wide claims handling
rubrics_metrics.description: No special search effort needs to be made when searching unduly wide or speculative claims, beyond the extent to which they are supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expand search into remote areas merely because of broad claim wording, unless it is probable that relevant documents could establish lack of novelty/inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims in search
rubrics_metrics.description: The search carried out for the independent claim(s) must also take into consideration the subject-matter of all dependent claims. Dependent claims are interpreted as being restricted by all features of the claim(s) upon which they depend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If novelty/inventive step of independent claim is apparent, further search on dependent claims may be unnecessary; expand search if main claim is questioned or dependent claim adds novel combination/features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search of particular claim types and parts (two‑part, preamble, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The words of a claim must be read as they would be understood by a PSIA. In two-part claims, the preamble is regarded as a limitation on the scope of the claim; in some circumstances it may be desirable to extend the search to include the technological background, preamble, or general state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include preamble/intro/background where relevant to find closest prior art or context; interpret claim terms as understood in the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination claims — search combinations and sub‑combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims characterised by a combination of elements (e.g., A, B and C), the search should be directed towards the combination; however, sub-combinations (AB, AC, BC) and individual elements should be searched in those units at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search additional classification units for sub-combinations only if necessary to establish novelty of an element or to assess inventive step of the combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different categories of claims — include all when unity satisfied
rubrics_metrics.description: When the application contains claims of different categories that comply with unity of invention, all these must be included in the search. When the application contains only claims of one category, it may be desirable to include other categories in the search (e.g., search product when process is claimed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cross-classified documents that may disclose aspects in another claim category; search final products in chemical/process cases unless evidently known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy preliminary steps (citations, inaccessible docs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents cited in the application should be examined if they are cited as the starting point of the invention or show the state of the art; if a cited document is not accessible and appears essential, the searching authority may request a copy from the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no copy is provided, attempt search and indicate if meaningful search could not be carried out as a whole or needed restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract, title and classification handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner considers the abstract (with title and figures) and should determine its definitive contents no later than completion of the search report; after considering the abstract, the examiner then classifies the application according to at least the IPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the abstract/title for initial orientation and classification; finalize before completing the search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search statement and unity considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may prepare a written search statement defining the subject of their search as precisely as possible. Considerations relating to exclusion from search and lack of unity of invention should be borne in mind; if unity is not satisfied, the examiner may choose to conduct a search on the first invention only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear search statement helps structure the search and justify any restrictions based on unity or practicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of the closest prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The closest prior art is that which in one single reference discloses the combination of features which constitutes the most promising starting point for a development leading to the invention. It should be directed to a similar purpose or effect or belong to the same or a closely related technical field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select closest prior art based on similarity of purpose/effect and examiner's interpretation of the claims; use it as basis for inventive-step analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to cite prior art aiding sufficiency/support
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner is encouraged to cite any prior art likely to be of assistance in determining sufficiency of description throughout the whole of the field claimed and the requirement that the claimed invention be fully supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite documents that illuminate whether the disclosure enables the claimed scope or supports claim features.
